focus: 壞消息要帶時間表，不是帶情緒
lead: 升級壞消息最容易犯的錯，不是不敢講，是講得太晚、太籠統，而且忍不住先撇清責任。今天練的是先講範圍、再講你扛的部分、最後給新時間表——你不是在道歉，你是在幫對方做決定。每個 speaking 段落請先出聲講完再看 model answer。

phrases.en: I want to flag this before it becomes a surprise on the 18th.
phrases.ex: I want to flag this before it becomes a surprise on the 18th — we have a calibration issue on three vehicles.
phrases.gl: 我想在這件事變成 18 號的驚喜之前先讓你知道（把「現在講」框成幫對方爭取時間，而不是丟包情緒）

phrases.en: This is on me — I signed off on that checklist Monday.
phrases.ex: This is on me — I signed off on that checklist Monday, so let me walk you through what I'm doing about it.
phrases.gl: 這是我的責任——checklist 是我週一簽核的（先承擔你能控制的部分，主管反而更信任你接下來講的話）

phrases.en: Here's what we know, here's what we don't, and here's what I'm doing about it.
phrases.ex: Here's what we know, here's what we don't, and here's what I'm doing about it — let me take these one at a time.
phrases.gl: 已知、未知、行動，三段式攤開壞消息（把恐慌感換成可以追蹤的結構,對方不會覺得你在瞞）

phrases.en: The realistic delivery date is the 23rd, not the 18th.
phrases.ex: Given the re-labeling scope, the realistic delivery date is the 23rd, not the 18th.
phrases.gl: 務實的交付日是 23 號，不是 18 號（新日期要講死、講具體，不要用 hopefully 這種詞削弱可信度）

phrases.en: I'd rather tell you now with five days of runway than surprise you next Friday.
phrases.ex: I'd rather tell you now with five days of runway than surprise you next Friday when the handoff is already late.
phrases.fix: 取代 “I'm sorry to say this but...”
phrases.gl: 我寧願現在講、留五天跑道，也不要下週五才讓你嚇一跳（把「早講」講成對他有利的選擇）

phrases.en: Two options: we ship 62% clean on the 18th, or all of it five days late.
phrases.ex: Two options: we ship 62% clean on the 18th, or all of it five days late — your call on which Perception needs more.
phrases.gl: 兩個選項：18 號先交 62% 乾淨的資料，或是全部晚五天（把決定權還給對方,你負責讓成本透明）

phrases.en: I need a decision from you by Friday on which trade-off you want.
phrases.ex: I need a decision from you by Friday on which trade-off you want, so I can tell Kevin's team today.
phrases.gl: 我需要你週五前給我一個關於取捨的決定（壞消息的結尾不能只是報告,要有明確的請求）

phrases.en: I'm not asking you to fix it. I'm asking you to know it.
phrases.ex: I'm not asking you to fix it. I'm asking you to know it, so nothing lands on your desk cold next week.
phrases.fix: 取代 “I don't know what to do, can you help”
phrases.gl: 我不是要你來解決,我是要你知情（讓主管清楚你不是在推工作給他,是在讓他能往上管理）

phrases.en: Here's the checklist change that makes this unlikely to repeat.
phrases.ex: Here's the checklist change that makes this unlikely to repeat — we're adding a drift check before every labeling handoff.
phrases.fix: 取代 “this will not happen again, I promise”
phrases.gl: 這是讓這件事不太可能再發生的 checklist 改動（用具體機制取代空泛保證,更誠實也更有說服力）

setup: Setup. Wednesday morning, routine calibration check. Three of eight data-collection vehicles show LiDAR misalignment beyond the 0.5-degree tolerance — drift that started roughly two weeks ago, around August 26th. Kevin's outsourcing team has already labeled about two weeks of SRDC data off those three vehicles: roughly 40,000 frames, 62% of this sprint's total dataset. The SRDC v0.0.3 handoff to Perception and Simulation is committed for September 18th, nine days out, and both teams have blocked their own sprints on it. You signed off on the calibration checklist yourself last Monday. David doesn't know any of this yet.

prompts.frame: 先講「現在講」的理由（幫他爭取跑道）→ 三段式攤開已知／未知／在做什麼 → 給新的可信日期 → 明講需要他做的決定。
prompts.model: “I want to flag this before it becomes a surprise on the 18th, not after. Here's what we know: three of eight vehicles drifted out of calibration around the 26th, and Kevin's team already labeled roughly 40,000 frames off those three — that's 62% of this sprint. Here's what we don't know yet: whether the drift affected the LiDAR-camera fusion labels or just the point cloud. Here's what I'm doing: Rick is re-running the calibration diff tonight, and I'll have the affected-frame count by tomorrow noon. Realistic delivery is the 23rd, not the 18th. This is on me — I signed off on that checklist Monday. What I need from you is a decision: hold the whole handoff for a clean dataset, or split it and send the unaffected 38% on the 18th.”
prompts.q: David: “Why are you telling me this now instead of waiting until you actually have a fix?”
prompts.say: 出聲講完整段（目標 55 秒）。第一句不准是 “I'm sorry” 開頭，第一句必須是 “I want to flag this before…” 這類的句型。

prompts.frame: 承認那是個選項 → 用數字講清楚趕工的代價（不要用「不可能」）→ 給一個更小、可驗證的替代方案 → 給評估後的回報時間。
prompts.model: “That's the first thing I checked. Kevin's team can physically push 40,000 frames through a weekend re-label — but their normal QA pass catches about 8% error on rushed batches, versus 2% on a standard pass. On fusion labels, that's the difference between usable and unusable for Perception's model. I'd rather ship half of this properly than all of it badly. So here's what I'll do instead: I'll get Rick to isolate exactly which frames the drift actually touched — my guess is it's fewer than the full 40,000, maybe closer to 15,000 — and Kevin's team only re-labels those, at normal QA speed. I'll have that isolated count by Thursday morning. That's a smaller ask and a real number, not a guess.”
prompts.q: David: “Can't Kevin's team just re-label the affected frames over the weekend so we still hit the 18th?”
prompts.say: 出聲練習「技術上婉拒趕工要求」。禁用 “not possible”、“no can do”。

prompts.frame: 給一句對外可以講的話 → 附上你正在做的具體行動與檢核點 → 明確下一次更新時間 → 書面收尾。
prompts.model: “Tell them this: ‘SRDC v0.0.3 slips from the 18th to the 23rd for a subset of frames tied to a calibration drift on three vehicles — root cause found, re-labeling in progress, full breakdown by Thursday noon.' That's specific enough that nobody thinks we're guessing. On my side: Rick isolates the affected frame count by tomorrow, I'll have a go or no-go on the split-delivery option by Thursday, and I'll send you and both leads a written update every day until this closes, not just when there's good news. If the isolated count comes back under 15,000 frames, I think we can still hit something close to the 18th for most of the dataset.”
prompts.q: David: “Okay — but I need to tell Perception and Simulation something today. What do I say?”
prompts.say: 練習「給主管一句可以往上傳的話」。禁用 “we'll try our best”、“as soon as possible”。

fixes.bad: I want to inform you that there is maybe some problem with calibration.
fixes.good: I need to flag a calibration problem — three of eight vehicles are affected.
fixes.note: Register（語氣強度）：“inform you that there is maybe” 太過婉轉，聽起來像在報告一件無關緊要的事。壞消息要用 flag，直接給範圍（3/8），語氣越明確，對方越信任你接下來的話。

fixes.bad: The vehicles has calibration issue since two weeks.
fixes.good: The vehicles have had a calibration issue for two weeks.
fixes.note: Grammar（主詞動詞一致＋時態）：vehicles 是複數要用 have；「持續到現在的狀態」要用 have had。since 後面接時間點（since August 26th），for 才接時間長度（for two weeks）。

fixes.bad: It's not my fault, the vendor made a mistake in labeling.
fixes.good: I signed off on the checklist Monday — that's on me, and the vendor's labeling is the downstream effect.
fixes.note: Register（究責語氣）：“not my fault” 是防衛姿態，聽在主管耳裡像在找代罪羔羊。先承擔你能控制的部分，反而讓你看起來更有掌控權、更可信。

fixes.bad: We will try to deliver until 23rd.
fixes.note: Preposition＋Collocation：until 用在「持續到」，deliver 是一次性完成動作要用 by。另外 try to deliver 聽起來沒把握——壞消息裡的新承諾要講死，不要留模糊空間。

fixes.bad: This will not happen again, I promise.
fixes.good: Here's the checklist change that makes this specific failure unlikely to repeat.
fixes.note: Credibility（可信度）：壞消息後的空泛保證（promise）沒有說服力，主管要聽的是具體機制，不是情緒保證。“unlikely to repeat” 也比 “will not happen again” 誠實，不會把話講死。

challenge:
今天遇到任何需要往上報的壞消息時，做這一件事：不要等到有完整解法才開口，先讓對方知道範圍與新時間表 ——

“I want to flag this before it becomes a surprise on ___. Here's what we know, here's what we don't, and here's what I'm doing about it. The realistic date is ___, not ___.”

錄音作業（60 秒，手機錄）：挑一件你這週「還沒跟主管講、但其實該講」的壞消息，講一次。

  • 第一句不能是道歉，要先講你為什麼現在講
  • 中段要有一個具體數字（受影響的比例、天數、數量）
  • 結尾一定要給對方一個新日期或新決定的請求，不能只是報告
  • 禁用：I'm sorry to say、this won't happen again、not my fault、we'll try our best、maybe
check: 我是不是等太久才把這個壞消息講出來？
我有沒有先講自己扛的部分，還是先怪別人？
我最後有沒有給對方一個具體的新日期或決定？
